questions.q: How did Roger Federer's path differ from Tiger Woods's?
a: He tried many sports before focusing on tennis
He began training seriously at age four
He specialized in one sport from childhood
He avoided coaches for most of his career
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Federer sampled skiing, basketball and other sports before settling on tennis.

questions.q: What made comic creators successful, according to the research?
a: Breadth of experience across many genres
The sheer number of comics they published
Access to bigger budgets and teams
A single, highly recognizable art style
questions.why: Lesson 2 found that working in more genres predicted success better than output or resources.

questions.q: What did Tetlock find about famous experts?
a: The more visible they were, the less accurate they became
They forecast better than amateurs over time
Media exposure sharpened their judgment
They were right whenever they felt certain
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the more an expert appeared on television, the more likely they were wrong.

questions.q: Why do experts make poor predictions, according to the summary?
a: Narrow focus leads them to cherry-pick evidence
They lack access to classified information
They change their minds too often to commit
They avoid making public statements
questions.why: Lesson 3 says specialists build explicit theories, then select evidence that confirms them.

questions.q: How do Nobel laureates differ from other scientists?
a: They are far more likely to pursue outside interests
They specialize earlier than their peers
They publish fewer papers overall
They avoid working across disciplines
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes laureates are many times more likely to also act, perform or create.
